newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE may climb to 4,880 after weak start.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE may climb to 4,880 after weak start.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index should manage to go a little higher on Tuesday attempting to reach 4,880 after a weak start which may take it to 4,850, technical analysts said.

Financial stocks and oil shares should help lift the index, they added. The market showed stirrings of strength on Monday when it made a higher intra-day low than the previous day and managed to finish the day on a positive note.
But this will not be sufficient to rouse too much buying interest so that any upward move by the market will be limited.
By 0734 GMT, the FTSE was down 4.4 at 4,858.2.

Monday's market action may have converted what at first sight appeared to be a downward sloping channel -- which had engulfed the FTSE's intra-day highs and lows over the past four days -- to a bullish wedge pattern.
Instead of a pair of parallel trendlines guiding the market lower, the trendlines in a bullish wedge pattern still have a downward slope but are converging.

But before convergence the market breaks upwards above the upper trendline. Breakout is usually accompanied by greater turnover -- and if breakout occurs today -- the total volume of shares traded should be greater than Monday's 647 million.
